questions.question: In a circle with centre O, an arc ABC subtends an angle of 110° at the centre of the circle. The chord AB is produced to a point P. Then ∠CBP is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/56107e6a0e3bf58520b9369646f18866ebdff464721e53a1b4dadde9cc454bcd.png] 

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is double the size of the angle subtended by the same arc at the circle circumference

Take any point Q on the circumference and join AQ and QC .

∴ ∠AOC = 2 × ∠AQC

⇒ ∠AQC = 1/2 × ∠AOC = 1/2 × 110° = 55°

Now, ∠CBP = ∠AQC [exterior angle of cyclic quadrilateral]

⇒ ∠CBP = 55°

questions.question:
In the given figure, B and C are the centres of two circles. ADE is the common tangent to the two circles. If ratio of the radius of both the circle is 3 : 5 and AC = 40, then what is the value of DE?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2f3bd1fbc41e6e9cc854b7bea92f0453b14f1fe4806c093190df5813db1c97f.png]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7106292b99721adc4a2e95a606cf745e9ff2fc0306f96381e94b1dcc5120611c.png] 

∆ABD ~ ∆ACE

⇒ BD/CE = AD/AE = AB/AC

⇒ 3x/5x = AD/AE = AB/40

⇒ AB = 24

∴ BC = 40 - 24 = 16

⇒ 3x + 5x = 16 we get x = 2

⇒ CE = 5x = 10

⇒ AE² = 40² - 10² = 1500

⇒ AE = √1500 = 10√15

So, DE = 2/5 × 10√15 = 4√15

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, PQR is a tangent at the point Q on it. AB is a chord in the circle parallel to the tangent such that ∠BQR = 70°. What is the measure of ∠AQB?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/63edd987bde9e60dde801d96e1f1bd6a69b084069aeefc17ce871b6485716682.png] 

⇒ ∠BQR = 70° (Given)

⇒ ∠BQR = ∠QBA = 70° (Alternate interior angle)

⇒ ∠BQR = ∠QAB = 70° (Alternate segment theorem)

In ΔAQB

⇒ ∠AQB + ∠QAB + ∠QBA = 180°

⇒ ∠AQB + 70° + 70° = 180°

⇒ ∠AQB = 180° – 140° = 40°

questions.question:
In the given figure, O is centre of the circle. Circle has 3 tangents. If ∠QPR = 45°, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠QOR?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29a59ad06241cfb5166654fad9d055855b8493d39b2dbe3fdce15d69d7b1c4da.png]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29a59ad06241cfb5166654fad9d055855b8493d39b2dbe3fdce15d69d7b1c4da.png] 

We know that tangents drawn from an external point to the circle are equal in length.

∴ QS = QT and RU = RT

∴ ∠SQO = ∠OQT = x and ∠TRO = ∠ORU = y (suppose)

Then ∠PQR = 180° – 2x and ∠PRQ = 180° – 2y 

In ΔPQR;

180° – 2x + 180° – 2y + 45° = 180°

⇒ 2(x + y) = 225°

⇒ (x + y) = 112.5°

Now in ΔOQR;

⇒ x + y + ∠QOR = 180° 

⇒ 112.5 + ∠QOR = 180°

⇒ ∠QOR = 67.5°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** ∠UOS = (180° - 45°) = 135°

 UR = RT, QS = QT (Since tangent to a circle from same external points were equal)

Also, OQ = OT = OR (Radii of the same circle)

∠UOR = ∠ROT and ∠TOQ = ∠QOS (Since Tangent from an external point subtend equal angles at the centre)

∠QOR = ∠ROT + ∠TOQ = 1/2 ∠SOT + 1/2 ∠TOU

∠QOR = 1/2 ∠UOS 

∠QOR = 1/2 × 135° = 67.5°

questions.question: A circle of a radius of 10 cm and another circle whose radius is 20% less than that of the first circle, intersect at points P and Q. If the length of PQ is 20% more than the radius of the first circle. The distance between the centres of the circle is x cm. What is the approximate value of x?
questions.solution:
Radius of the first circle OP = 10 cm

Radius of the other circle O’P = 10 × [80/100] = 8 cm

Length of PQ = 10 × [120/100] = 12 cm

As we know, PM = PQ/2, PM = 6 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1b4c5529db85c449d828f7c2f70036fdec1b3d726283f0243c2bfbd017e4daf8.png] 

In ΔPO’M

By using Pythagoras Theorem

⇒ (O’P)² = (O’M)² + (PM)²

⇒ 8² = (O’M)² + 6²

⇒ O’M = √28 cm

In ΔPOM

By using Pythagoras Theorem

⇒ (OP)² = (OM)² + (PM)²

⇒ 10² = (OM)² + 6²

⇒ OM = 8 cm

⇒ O’O = OM + O’M = √28 + 8 = 5.3 + 8 = 13.3 c

questions.question: In a circle having radius 17 cm, what is the distance between two parallel chords each of 30 cm?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4eda6b3fb0f78f0bf80011e1a7930bbb71f2cd7c451f62b6ce68c9c27a5bb4a6.png] 

DE and FG are two parallel chords of length 30 cm.

In ΔHCE we get,

⇒ HE = DE/2 = 15 cm

⇒ CE = 17 cm

∴ HC,

⇒ √(17² – 15²)

⇒ √(289 – 225)

⇒ 8 cm

In ΔICG we get,

⇒ IG = FG/2 = 15 cm

⇒ CG = 17 cm

∴ CI,

⇒ √(17² – 15²)

⇒ √(289 – 225)

⇒ 8 cm

∴ Distance between the chords, HI →

⇒ HC + CI

⇒ 8 + 8

⇒ 16 cm

questions.question:
A ΔSQR is made inside the circle, a tangent is drawn to a circle from an outside point P, then find the perimeter of ΔPRS, if perimeter of ΔPQS is 46 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5cfa2d9396a61a5bca684277bbdf0cf3aa95c7b191fe493313f32e2a10c5b5c0.png]
questions.solution:
Let QP be ‘x’ cm

⇒ PS² = PQ × PR

⇒ 18² = x × (x + 15)

⇒ QP, x = 12 cm

Perimeter of ΔPQS is 46 cm

⇒ PQ + SP + SQ = 46

⇒ SQ = 16 cm

In ΔPQS and ΔPSR,

∠P is common

∠PSQ = ∠PRS (Angles in the alternate segment)

∠PQS = ∠PSR

⇒ ΔPQS and ΔPSR are similar

⇒ SQ/SR = PQ/PS

⇒ SQ/SR = 12/18

⇒ SR = 16 × 18/12 = 24 cm

∴ Perimeter of ΔPRS = 69 cm
